newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-DUNWOODY WARMS UP WITH AINTREE TREBLE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DUNWOODY WARMS UP WITH AINTREE TREBLE.

text.p: Richard Dunwoody, twice a winner of the Grand National, warmed up for Saturday's big race with three successes on Friday.

On the second day of Aintree's three-day-festival, victories on favourites Sanmartino (8-11) and Cyborgo (13-8) were topped off by a game success in the last race on top weight Unguided Missile, the 7-2 second favourite.
Dunwoody, who won the National in 1986 on West Tip and again three years ago on Miinnehoma, partners Jenny Pitman's 16-1 chance Smiths Band in Saturday's race.
The big obstacles and four-and-a-half mile (7.2 km) test of stamina may suit Smith's Band but Dunwoody has yet to ride the horse.
"I'll be sitting on him for the first time tomorrow morning (during training), said the jockey. "Jenny's getting us out of bed early."
Veteran trainer Tim Forster, who first won the National 25 years ago with Well To Do, also had a winner on Friday when the day's most valuable race went to the classy Martha's Son.
Forster, who went on to win two more Nationals with Ben Nevis in 1980 and Last Suspect five years later, is doubly represented on Saturday by General Wolfe (20-1) and River Mandate (40-1).
If either battles half as well as Martha's Son in the two-and-a-half mile (4-km) Melling Chase, their chances would have to be respected.
Martha's Son, who missed the entire 1996 season, won last month's two-mile (3.2 km) Queen Mother Champion Chase in one of the highlights of the Cheltenham Festival, beating a top quality field.
On Friday the horse, ridden by Carl Llewellyn, repeated the dose, brushing aside a stumble at the first to come home five lengths clear of high-class perfomers Strong Promise and Viking Flagship.
Forster, 62, said: "He's got two speeds -- one idling and then he turns on the fireburners and he's off."
The going is forecast good for the 150th National on Saturday when the grey Suny Bay is likely to start favourite at around 8-1.
Jamie Osborne, the horse's jockey, gave up a couple of rides in later races on Friday but is expected to be fine on Saturday.
Course doctor Mike Murray said: "He's a bit shaken up from earlier falls but it's nothing serious."
